Package com.datastax.oss.driver.api.querybuilder.condition

Interface ConditionalStatement<SelfT extends ConditionalStatement<SelfT>>

  • All Known Subinterfaces:
    Delete, Update
    public interface ConditionalStatement<SelfT extends ConditionalStatement<SelfT>>
    A statement that can be applied conditionally, such as UPDATE or DELETE.

    Not that this does not covert INSERT... IF NOT EXISTS, which is handled separately.

    • Method Detail

      • ifExists

        @NonNull
@CheckReturnValue
SelfT ifExists()
        Adds an IF EXISTS condition.

        If any column conditions were added before, they will be cleared.

      • if_

        @NonNull
@CheckReturnValue
SelfT if_​(@NonNull
          Condition condition)
        Adds an IF condition. All conditions are logically joined with AND. If ifExists() was invoked on this statement before, it will get cancelled.

        To create the argument, use one of the factory methods in Condition, for example column.

        If you add multiple conditions as once, consider if_(Iterable) as a more efficient alternative.

      • if_

        @NonNull
@CheckReturnValue
SelfT if_​(@NonNull
          Iterable<Condition> conditions)
        Adds multiple IF conditions at once. All conditions are logically joined with AND. If ifExists() was invoked on this statement before, it will get cancelled.

        This is slightly more efficient than adding the relations one by one (since the underlying implementation of this object is immutable).

        To create the arguments, use one of the factory methods in Condition, for example column.

      • ifRaw

        @NonNull
@CheckReturnValue
default SelfT ifRaw​(@NonNull
                    String raw)
        Adds a raw CQL snippet as a condition.

        This is the equivalent of creating a condition with QueryBuilder.raw(String) and passing it to if_(Condition).

        The contents will be appended to the query as-is, without any syntax checking or escaping. This method should be used with caution, as it's possible to generate invalid CQL that will fail at execution time; on the other hand, it can be used as a workaround to handle new CQL features that are not yet covered by the query builder.

        See Also:
        QueryBuilder.raw(String)
